answer: A proof-of-inference protocol resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to solve verifiable compute tasks to register. Nodes must process complex inputs—such as imagery of a wharf, lidar of a canyon, or meter in a sonnet—and return cryptographic execution receipts. An attacker must expend scarce GPU cycles and power per identity, making mass spoofing cost-prohibitive. However, this mechanism adds verification latency and penalizes legitimate, low-resource agents.
